items.title: Barcelona riots fuel tensions before November election
items.body: Barcelona's October 24 riots led to 128 arrests and 23 looted shops. The unrest has fuelled unfounded accusations between parties ahead of the November 29 general election. Social media groups are calling for further gatherings on October 31.

items.title: ECB expected to hold rates amid French turmoil
items.body: Economists expect the European Central Bank to keep its benchmark rate at 2.5% at its meeting in the week of October 26. French debt turmoil has tightened financial conditions and is cooling demand. The French 10-year bond has climbed to 5%, a level not seen since the euro began in 2002.

items.title: Food price rises outstrip wage growth in Spain
items.body: Food prices have risen 31.8% since December 2021, compared with 20.7% growth in gross pay per employee. That gap explains why groceries still strain household budgets even as food inflation slows. September's annual food price rise was 2.7%, below overall inflation of 4.9%.

items.title: Inflation-linked pay clauses cover 3.64 million workers
items.body: Wage guarantee clauses cover 3.64 million employees, or 19% of workers registered with Social Security. These clauses provide extra pay as prices rise; 1.3 million workers have retroactive protection. Higher energy and fuel prices are also pushing up employers' costs.

items.title: Brookfield seeks buyers for 1,550 Madrid rental homes
items.body: Brookfield is seeking to sell about 1,550 Madrid rental homes bought from Blackstone in April. Experts doubt a deal will close amid uncertainty over post-election rules. The government will take the so-called "decreto Maricarmen" to Congress's standing committee.

items.title: Doctors' strikes spread from October 28
items.body: Unions cancelled the national doctors' strike planned for October 30 after the election call caused the disputed health-worker statute to lapse. Regional strikes continue: the Canary Islands began first, Madrid, Catalonia, and the Valencia region join on October 28, and Andalusia in November. The five regions hold 64% of Spain's population.

items.title: Valencia race delivers two Spanish half-marathon records
items.body: Burundi-born Spanish runner Rodrigue Kwizera set a national half-marathon record of 58m 3s in Valencia. It cannot count as a European record because he has not yet received the World Athletics document he needs to compete as a Spaniard. Runner Laura Luengo also set a Spanish record.

items.title: Montseny bus crash leaves seven seriously injured
items.body: Seven people suffered serious injuries when a bus fell down a 20-metre embankment in Fogars de Montclús on October 25. Firefighters searched overnight for anyone still missing. The BV-5114 is closed between kilometre points 3 and 25, from Fogars de Montclús to Arbúcies.

items.title: Madrid courts reject neighbours' bid to ban coliving
items.body: Two final Madrid court rulings found that a building's ban on tourist flats did not cover coliving room rentals. Neighbours failed to prove noise or nuisance. The judges said banning this type of rental would require a unanimous change to the building's community rules.

items.title: Pension industry pushes for automatic workplace enrolment
items.body: Pension managers and insurers are calling for automatic enrolment in workplace pension plans ahead of the November 29 election. This remains an industry proposal, not a new requirement for workers. Political and social agreement remains distant.

items.title: Prosecutors seek embezzlement charge over Zapatero's jewels
items.body: Prosecutors want to charge former prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero with embezzlement over undeclared jewels initially valued at €1.3 million. His official list of nearly 500 gifts included no jewellery. The investigating judge requested a certified record on October 23.

items.title: Older workers account for over 1.1 million terminations
items.body: Older workers accounted for more than 1.1 million job terminations in five years, with 56% affecting people aged 45 to 54. The article says companies cut costs by shedding older, better-paid staff and use layoffs to make their workforces younger.

items.title: Film director José Luis García Sánchez dies aged 85
items.body: Film director José Luis García Sánchez died in Madrid on October 25, aged 85, the Spanish Film Academy confirmed. His nearly 60-year career included two screenwriting Goyas and the Berlin Golden Bear for Las truchas.

items.title: Hospitality tips count as taxable employment income
items.body: Under the IRPF (personal income tax) law, hospitality workers must declare tips as income. Employers distributing shared tips must withhold tax; if they control distribution, tips also count for Social Security contributions. Tips do not affect VAT.

items.title: Free app alerts users to immigration appointment slots
items.body: Extranjería App sends free Android and iPhone alerts when immigration appointment slots open across Spanish provinces. It can help with NIE (foreigner identification number) or TIE (foreigner identity card) renewals and other procedures. Users must still book through the official service after receiving an alert.
